item.title: Development :: RE: New programming language MasterBASIC
item.description:
Author: Tom
Posted: Fri Nov 06, 2026 8:18 am (GMT 0)

Because some people actually like Basic. As much as I can program in C and even C# if I'm forced to, Basic is always going to feel more natural to me. Everything I released around here over the years, such as the Slider editor, has been programmed in Visual Basic 5 (and would work in both Windows 95 and 11 without much fuss). I'll never get the point of this obsession with "modern" things. If something works, let it work.

I don't know where this is going, and I doubt I'm actually going to use this, because I don't have the motivation to keep up at this point of my life (I barely even post anymore, both here and on Sonic Retro), but I'm sure there are other Basic enthusiasts out there.

Let people have different preferences.

item.description:
Author: Bits Passats
Posted: Fri Nov 06, 2026 6:32 am (GMT 0)

Disclaimer: the 'b', 'n', 'm' in my laptop's keyboard are jammed, so if you see multiple of them when they shouldn't or an absence of them, it is for this reason. I revise and correct, but I am human and something might escape the revision. Thanks for your comprehension.

KalexPidd wrote
Bits Passats wrote

And the Catalan flag has four red stripes, not three like Twitter/X pretends


When did X pretend that the Catalan flag has three red stripes? This is a genuine question, I'm not trying to spark any debate.


Hello

The "when", I don't know exactly since when did they apply their emoji designs. But there's the "how".

La Senyera does not appear as a standalone flag, as Catalonia is not a country. However it appears as an embedded flag in the coat of arms of other flags. Flags like Andorra and Spain.

The Andorran coat of arms is formed by four quarters, each two of them represent one of the sides of the signatories of the Pariages from the XIIIth Century (the fundational documents of the country). There are the two cows of Béarn (the ones that got us that small moment of joy when in The Big Bang Theory made a joke about us in Fun With Flags), the Bishop's mitra, the Foix flag (which consists in three red stripes over a yellow background) and finally but not least (I left it for last basically to emphatize it, it is usually the first to be told) La Senyera, which should consist in four red stripes over a yellow background. However, the graphic designers at X/Twitter lazily copied the Foix flag again.

So, in X/Twitter the Andorran flag is defaced. And it is defaced because La Senyera is defaced. Will they change it? I don't know. We are small and easy to ignore.

Again I insist, sybols are graphs which have a eaning behind them. Not all symbols are of equal importance. Flags represent people, and getting them wrong will certainly anger people. So, as with other sybols, flags need a special care when handling.

Thank you for asking. Have a nice day!

item.title: Main :: Kujaku Ou — Brazilian Portuguese Translation and Restoration for Sega Mark III / Master System
item.description:
Author: cristiano.mariano
Subject: Kujaku Ou — Brazilian Portuguese Translation and Restoration for Sega Mark III / Master System
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 1:26 pm (GMT 0)

Hello everyone,

I am Cristiano Mariano from Newportgame, and this is my Brazilian Portuguese translation and technical restoration of Kujaku Ou (孔雀王) for the Sega Mark III / Sega Master System.

Kujaku Ou was originally released by Sega in Japan in 1988. It later received a heavily adapted western version known as SpellCaster, which changed several names, characters, cultural references, locations, magical concepts, and parts of the original narrative.

This project was translated directly from the Japanese version to preserve the original identity and context of the game. It restores the story of Kujaku, the young Buddhist exorcist, together with the original mythological, religious, historical, and geographical references.

The project includes:

- Complete Brazilian Portuguese translation based on the Japanese version;
- Dialogues, menus, status screens, items, credits, and ending;
- Translation and integration of the original manga-style ending;
- Native Brazilian Portuguese accent support;
- Restoration of original names, places, characters, and cultural references;
- Technical validation in emulators and on real hardware.

The work involved reverse engineering of the Z80 code, VDP and VRAM routines, text encoding, font data, pointer tables, banked ROM structures, graphics data, and the game's text-space limitations. Since Portuguese generally requires more space than Japanese, the internal text structure had to be reorganized so the complete translation could fit without forced abbreviations.

This project does not diminish SpellCaster, which has its own identity and historical value. SpellCaster is a western adaptation with shorter and more accessible fantasy-oriented dialogue, while Kujaku Ou preserves the original Japanese cultural and spiritual context. Both versions are now available in Brazilian Portuguese, each with its own purpose and character.

PROJECT INFORMATION

Game: Kujaku Ou (孔雀王 / Peacock King)
Platform: Sega Mark III / Sega Master System
Original release: 1988
Genre: First-person adventure, 2D action/platforming, and RPG elements
Original developer/publisher: Sega
Original source: The Kujaku Ou manga by Makoto Ogino
Patch version: v1.0.0 — Gold Master
Translator and technical restoration: Cristiano Mariano
Project: Newportgame

BASE ROM INFORMATION

The patch must be applied to an original, clean, compatible Japanese ROM.

Recommended filename: Kujaku Ou (Japan).sms
ROM size: 524,288 bytes (512 KB)
Patch format: IPS

The original commercial ROM is not distributed with this project.

OFFICIAL DOWNLOAD

GitHub release:
https://github.com/contatonewportgame-code/kujaku-ou-sms-ptbr/releases/tag/v1.0....

Direct IPS download:
https://github.com/contatonewportgame-code/kujaku-ou-sms-ptbr/releases/download/...

HOW TO APPLY THE PATCH

1. Open Rom Patcher JS:
https://www.marcrobledo.com/RomPatcher.js/

2. Select the original Japanese ROM in the “ROM file” field.
3. Select KujakuOu_PTBR_Newportgame.ips in the “Patch file” field.
4. Click “Apply patch” and save the translated ROM.

The patch can also be applied with Lunar IPS or Floating IPS (Flips).

TOOLS AND ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS

The project used custom Python tools developed by Newportgame for ROM analysis, text extraction, pointer reconstruction, font investigation, memory expansion, and validation. Emulicious was used for low-level debugging, including Z80 debugging, memory inspection, tilemap analysis, and VRAM investigation.

AI tools were used only as assistance for calculations, consultations, and repetitive tasks. Translation decisions, technical direction, revisions, testing, and final validation were performed manually by Cristiano Mariano.

The project distributes only the IPS patch and related documentation. Complete ROM images are not distributed.

Thank you to everyone involved in the preservation, documentation, translation, reverse engineering, and study of classic Sega hardware and software.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Português:

Olá, pessoal!

Sou Cristiano Mariano, da Newportgame, e esta é minha tradução para português brasileiro e restauração técnica de Kujaku Ou (孔雀王) para Sega Mark III / Sega Master System.

Kujaku Ou foi lançado originalmente pela Sega no Japão em 1988. Posteriormente, recebeu uma versão ocidental bastante adaptada, conhecida como SpellCaster, que alterou nomes, personagens, referências culturais, locais, conceitos mágicos e partes da narrativa original.

Este projeto foi traduzido diretamente da versão japonesa para preservar a identidade e o contexto originais do jogo. A tradução resgata a história de Kujaku, o jovem monge budista especializado em exorcismo, juntamente com as referências mitológicas, religiosas, históricas e geográficas presentes na obra original.

O projeto inclui:

- Tradução completa para português brasileiro baseada na versão japonesa;
- Diálogos, menus, telas de status, itens, créditos e encerramento;
- Tradução e integração do final original apresentado em formato de mangá;
- Suporte nativo aos acentos do português brasileiro;
- Restauração de nomes, locais, personagens e referências culturais originais;
- Validação técnica em emuladores e hardware real.

O trabalho envolveu engenharia reversa do código Z80, rotinas da VDP e da VRAM, codificação de texto, dados de fontes, tabelas de ponteiros, estruturas de bancos de ROM, dados gráficos e as limitações de espaço do texto no jogo. Como o português geralmente exige mais espaço que o japonês, foi necessário reorganizar a estrutura interna dos textos para inserir a tradução completa sem abreviações forçadas.

Este projeto não pretende diminuir SpellCaster, que possui identidade e valor histórico próprios. SpellCaster é uma adaptação ocidental, com diálogos mais curtos e uma abordagem de fantasia mais universal, enquanto Kujaku Ou preserva o contexto cultural e espiritual japonês original. Agora, ambas as versões estão disponíveis em português brasileiro, cada uma com sua própria proposta.

INFORMAÇÕES DA ROM-BASE

O patch deve ser aplicado a uma ROM japonesa original, limpa e compatível.

Nome recomendado: Kujaku Ou (Japan).sms
Tamanho: 524.288 bytes (512 KB)
Formato do patch: IPS

A ROM comercial original não é distribuída com este projeto.

DOWNLOAD OFICIAL

Página do release no GitHub:
https://github.com/contatonewportgame-code/kujaku-ou-sms-ptbr/releases/tag/v1.0....

Download direto do IPS:
https://github.com/contatonewportgame-code/kujaku-ou-sms-ptbr/releases/download/...

COMO APLICAR O PATCH

1. Acesse o Rom Patcher JS:
https://www.marcrobledo.com/RomPatcher.js/

2. Selecione a ROM japonesa original no campo “ROM file”.
3. Selecione KujakuOu_PTBR_Newportgame.ips no campo “Patch file”.
4. Clique em “Apply patch” e salve a ROM traduzida.

O patch também pode ser aplicado com Lunar IPS ou Floating IPS (Flips).

FERRAMENTAS E AGRADECIMENTOS

O projeto utilizou ferramentas próprias em Python, desenvolvidas pela Newportgame para análise de ROM, extração de textos, reconstrução de ponteiros, investigação de fontes, expansão de memória e validação. O Emulicious foi utilizado para depuração de baixo nível, incluindo análise do Z80, inspeção de memória, investigação de tilemaps e análise de VRAM.

Ferramentas de inteligência artificial foram utilizadas apenas como apoio para cálculos, consultas e tarefas repetitivas. As decisões de tradução, a direção técnica, as revisões, os testes e a validação final foram realizados manualmente por Cristiano Mariano.

O projeto distribui somente o patch IPS e a documentação relacionada. ROMs completas não são distribuídas.

Agradeço a todos que contribuem para a preservação, documentação, tradução, engenharia reversa e pesquisa de hardware e software clássicos da Sega.

item.description:
Author: Materion
Posted: Thu Nov 05, 2026 6:35 am (GMT 0)

Update 1.5.0

https://github.com/MaterzokMateusz/MasterBASIC/releases/tag/Release1.5

MasterBASIC 1.5.0 can now load music from text files: each song or sound effect can live in its own .txt file. The Master System has no disk, so the files are read when you build the game and copied into the cartridge; the game can’t load new files while it runs.

MUSIC theme = "music/theme.txt" ' one song per text file
MUSIC fanfare = "music/fanfare.txt" ONCE ' a jingle that plays once
SFX boing = "music/boing.txt" ' one sound effect per text file
SOUND "music/more.pml" ' a file with many songs (can be used several times)

PLAYMUSIC theme
PLAYSFX boing
